How this is built
WITS carries no all-Africa aggregate, and its Middle East & North Africa group cannot stand in for North Africa. But the service will serve
group-to-group: reporter/ssf/partner/ssf returns a value. Africa-wide intra-trade is therefore assembled from four blocks — Sub-Saharan to
Sub-Saharan, Sub-Saharan to North Africa, North Africa to Sub-Saharan, and the North African pairs — with Algeria and Libya, which file
nothing, recovered from what their African partners report importing from them. Shaded rows are the recovered and mirror-sourced parts.
This figure is a lower bound
The recovery works for Algeria and Libya because they are addressable as separate reporters. It cannot be done for Angola, DR Congo,
Congo-Brazzaville, Equatorial Guinea or Sudan, which sit inside the SSF aggregate and cannot be pulled out of it. Their intra-African flows
are therefore missing from the numerator while their exports are missing from the denominator too, so the bias is not one-directional —
but DR Congo in particular is a large regional trader, and the true share is above the figure shown.
Basis
This table is export-basis direct data. Tables 0 and 2 are mirror data. The denominators differ (US$590bn here against
US$681bn there), so the 16.5 per cent is not comparable with the China and seven-coloniser shares without rebasing first.
On the same construction, 2019 gives 18.3 per cent, though Algeria could not be recovered for that year, so it is a floor rather than an estimate.
